name: Deeper theory for better representations
gist: Papers provide mathematical foundations using variational inference, Riemannian geometry, and information theory to understand why certain representation learning methods work and how to improve them.
explain: Why does contrastive learning work? What guarantees does a representation satisfy? How many unlabeled examples do you need before representations converge to the truth? These questions live in theory. Papers here provide mathematical foundations: probabilistic frameworks explain why certain training goals lead to good representations, the mathematics of curved spaces shows how space shape affects what patterns can be encoded, information theory bounds how much data you need and predicts which methods should work best. Theory does not always lead to practical improvements, but it builds intuition and can reveal failure modes.

Theoretical work is hard because neural networks are nonconvex and complex — most analysis requires approximations or focuses on simpler settings (linear networks, infinite width limits, or highly structured data). Researchers study what properties a 'good' representation should have: sufficient information (capturing everything relevant for downstream tasks), disentanglement (different factors of variation are separable), or invariance (insensitivity to irrelevant transformations). Some papers prove that certain algorithms converge to true solutions or characterize the sample complexity: how the number of examples needed scales with dimension, number of classes, or noise level.

Across 11 papers, researchers build theoretical foundations for contrastive learning, self-supervised clustering, multimodal alignment, and continual learning. Some papers study loss surfaces: which optimization algorithms avoid bad local minima? Others study generalization: proving that models that fit training data well will transfer to new data. The work is often technical (heavy math) but yields insights: contrastive methods work because they maximize information between views so the model must capture what is stable across views, clustering works because it approximates the true density structure so categories emerge naturally, and transfer learning works because upstream and downstream tasks share underlying factors of variation. These insights guide practitioners in designing better methods and setting hyperparameters because they understand which design choices matter theoretically.

papers.title: Batch Normalization for Neural Networks on Complex Domains
papers.contribution: Experiments on radar clutter classification, node classification, and action recognition demonstrate efficacy of complex domain batch normalization.

papers.title: CARL: Preserving Causal Structure in Representation Learning
papers.contribution: CARL achieves state-of-the-art performance in preserving conditional independence patterns under synthetic experiments with known causal ground truth.

papers.title: Toward Scalable and Valid Conditional Independence Testing with Spectral Representations
papers.contribution: Links representation learning error to test performance with asymptotic validity and power guarantees, offering a principled path toward scalable CI testing bridging kernel-based theory with modern representation learning.

papers.title: Variational Deep Learning via Implicit Regularization
papers.contribution: Demonstrates strong in- and out-of-distribution performance without additional hyperparameter tuning and minimal computational overhead.

papers.title: AP-OOD: Attention Pooling for Out-of- Distribution Detection
papers.contribution: Reduces FPR95 from 27.77% to 5.91% on XSUM and from 75.19% to 68.13% on WMT15 En-Fr, setting state-of-the-art OOD detection for text.

papers.title: Amortized Variational Inference for Partial-Label Learning: A Probabilistic Approach to Label Disambiguation
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and efficiency on synthetic and real-world partial-label datasets.

papers.title: Controlled Dynamics Attractor Transformer
papers.contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art performance on graph anomaly detection and graph classification benchmarks.

papers.title: Fine-Tune Once, Reuse Across Models: Bayesian Task-Update Factors and Approximations
papers.contribution: We instead adopt a Bayesian-updating perspective: a base model defines a prior, while fine-tuning contributes a task-update factor that is prior-agnostic, thereby making it feasible to reuse the update across base models.

papers.title: Hyperbolic RQ-VAE enhanced Generative Recommendation with Differential-Length Codebook Strategy
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with lower collision rates, more uniform codebook usage, and reduced training time across benchmark datasets.

papers.title: Local Covariate Selection for Average Causal Effect Estimation without Pretreatment and Causal Sufficiency Assumptions
papers.contribution: The proposed method is both sound and complete under standard assumptions, enabling nonparametric causal effect estimation without global structure learning.

papers.title: Von Mises-Fisher Mixture Model with Dynamic Shrinkage for Realistic Test-Time Transduction
papers.contribution: Model-agnostic, training-free method that suppresses unreliable assignments and prevents harmful updates from outlier classes, mitigating negative transfer while improving efficiency.
